title: Blizzard Hasn't Shared WoW's Player Count Since 2015
hook: Blizzard's last official World of Warcraft subscriber count was 5.5 million in November 2015, down from 12 million at the 2010 peak. This month it called WoW Forever its biggest launch ever, with no number attached. Do you think more people play WoW now than in 2015?
script: Did you know nobody outside Blizzard has known how many people play World of Warcraft for more than a decade? In October 2010, Blizzard announced that WoW had passed twelve million subscribers. That was the peak. Over the next five years the number slid. On November 3rd, 2015, Activision Blizzard reported five and a half million subscribers, the lowest figure since 2005. Then it added a line that surprised everyone. That quarter would be the last time it ever shared subscriber numbers. The company said other metrics were better indicators of how Blizzard was doing. It has kept its word. Every expansion since then has launched without an official subscriber count. Fans have guessed from server queues, Twitch viewers and surveys, but Blizzard has never confirmed a number. That makes this month interesting. On November 4th, Blizzard launched World of Warcraft Forever. It is a third version of the game, built on the Azeroth of 2004 with new quests and stories. Three days later Blizzard said it was the biggest launch in WoW history by peak concurrent players, with more returning players than ever before. It still did not say how many. Do you think WoW has more players today than it did in 2015? Follow for more gaming history.
